059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.name: Benediction Room
059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.description:
The Benediction Room at the centre of the royal palace appears to be part of the Basilica as it has the same polychrome marble decoration.  
It symbolises the divine origins of Absolute Kingship, to whose authority even the Church submitted. From this room over the Basilica, the Royal Family attended mass, and from the veranda (on the opposite side) opening onto the square, King João V blessed his subjects.
059edbc5-9442-564e-ae32-2efb3b02e0ba.location: In the middle of the Royal Palace

073a3608-7fb8-5a06-99a1-807b858158d2.name: Chapel of Mercy, interior
073a3608-7fb8-5a06-99a1-807b858158d2.description: At the start of the comprehensive Baroque refurbishment work the master builder Gallus Gratl from Inzig erected a Chapel of Mercy on an oval ground plan at the site where, according to legend, herdsman worshipped the miracle-working image of the Virgin Mary, a small clothed statue of the Mother of God from the period around 1400. Piers with pilaster projections support a domical vault, interspersed with open semi-circular arches; in the cupola there is an oval opening. The Chapel of Mercy is thus to be understood as a homage to the Roman Pantheon which has been a Church of Mary since the 6th century.
073a3608-7fb8-5a06-99a1-807b858158d2.location: West nave, axial in the centre

08354b10-1797-50b3-80a2-2aabc67c1881.name: Church interior viewed from the choir
08354b10-1797-50b3-80a2-2aabc67c1881.description: Gilded woodcarving on the triumphal arch and main altar retable.
08354b10-1797-50b3-80a2-2aabc67c1881.artist: André Soares (1720–1769), Friar José de Santo António Vilaça (1731–1809) and others

0ae494ef-cd06-5be1-a894-e8f72b874300.name: Holy Trinity Column
0ae494ef-cd06-5be1-a894-e8f72b874300.description: A hexagonal stepped base carries a trilateral concave pedestal the columns of which support a sculpture of God the Father, Christ in heaven, and a pyramid crowned with the symbol of the Holy Spirit on a radial halo. The statues of the Immaculata and the saints are by the court sculptor, Lengelacher, after the painter, A. J. Prenner. The bottom section features allegories of Love, Faith and Hope, and emblems of the patrons.
0ae494ef-cd06-5be1-a894-e8f72b874300.artist: Anton Josef Prenner (1683 Wallerstein – 1761 Wien) – Ignaz Lengelacher (1698 Unter Peissenberg – 1780 Baden)

0ca8f01a-192f-5192-af7d-85d181189024.name: *St. Ignatius in Heavenly Glory*
0ca8f01a-192f-5192-af7d-85d181189024.description: For this painting, Garcia was inspired by the composition which Cirro Ferri (1634–1689) painted on the dome of the church St Agnese in Rome. Both works were based on the experience and compositional patterns of Pietro da Cortona (1596–1669).
0ca8f01a-192f-5192-af7d-85d181189024.location: Ceiling of the sanctuary, Jesuit Church of St Ignatius

0d0e56db-22c0-5b6c-94fa-3c424bf11d56.name: The Choir or Sala do Tesouro
0d0e56db-22c0-5b6c-94fa-3c424bf11d56.description: Probably used by the nuns as a meeting place, the floor is of inlaid Brazilian wood. The chapel contains several reliquaries within gilded wooden frames above the choir stalls. Above one of the doors there is a tabernacle with the coat of arms of King José I. The Window bays are adorned with *azulejos*, while the ceiling and walls are decorated with paintings of the Life of Christ and the Life of the Virgin Mary of the 17th and 18th centuries.
0d0e56db-22c0-5b6c-94fa-3c424bf11d56.artist: Marcos da Cruz [n.d.], Bento Coelho da Silveira (1648–1708), André Gonçalves (1685–1762)

0dbd6f4d-41ee-5eab-8782-2834ac28c4e6.name: Staircase
0dbd6f4d-41ee-5eab-8782-2834ac28c4e6.description: Passalacqua inventively reinterpreted the Roman town plan for use in Dubrovnik. With a convex–concave, axially conceived staircase space (in the axis of which is the entrance to the college) he created a deep scenic vista, with which in a distinctive Late Baroque manner, he integrated the Jesuit complex into the structure of the city. Extensive demolition of existing houses was necessary to accommodate the staircase and to widen the street for access. Thanks to Passalacqua’s staircase, the Jesuit complex in Dubrovnik is considered as the highest quality example of Baroque architecture and town planning on the Croatian Adriatic coast.
0dbd6f4d-41ee-5eab-8782-2834ac28c4e6.location: Jesuit Church of St Ignatius, college and Jesuit stairs

0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.name: Chapel of the Sorrowful Mother (Fieger Chapel)
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.description: Built as an extension to the vestibule, it was donated Johann Karl Graf Fieger. Together with the magnificent column altar, the most significant feature is the ceiling frescos from Kaspar Waldmann, a glorification of Mary with the seven founders of the Servite Order and scenes from the life of Mary.
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.location: Northern vestibule, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

0f4907e8-1bfe-5be4-9774-f6308f10d7a4.name: Pulpit
0f4907e8-1bfe-5be4-9774-f6308f10d7a4.description: Dark-bated oak pulpit with busts depicting Jesus Christ, the Virgin Mary and Saints Cajetan and Andreas Avellinus.

1174b2ab-da5e-56fc-b6bc-cc3311897b6b.name: Mount of Olives
1174b2ab-da5e-56fc-b6bc-cc3311897b6b.description: Behind the high altar is a grotto, “the Garden of Gethsemane”, with a relief sculpture of Christ and the Apostles on the Mount of Olives before Christ was tortured. A group of sinners suffering in purgatory are depicted on a tomb to accentuate His role as Saviour.
1174b2ab-da5e-56fc-b6bc-cc3311897b6b.location: High altar, Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka

131a9aab-cb29-5c8a-b6c9-6c0c8354e020.name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
131a9aab-cb29-5c8a-b6c9-6c0c8354e020.description: A statue of the Patron Saint of Wisdom, from the altar of the Holy Family, accompanies a canvas by M. Unterberger. W. Träger, who created the sculpted decoration for all the altars in the church, was a lesser-known pupil of O. Zahner with whom he worked from the 1740s. After his teacher’s death, Träger finished the Holy Trinity Column in Olomouc. His work in the Piarist Church in Mikulov complements an interior renowned, in particular, for a fresco by F. A. Maulbertsch. Träger was mainly active in Olomouc where he took over the workshop of J. A. Richter.

15bbc895-ece1-5072-8a0d-58528b3db808.name: Altar of the Holy Cross
15bbc895-ece1-5072-8a0d-58528b3db808.description: The stucco decoration of the altars and the pulpit was created by a prominent Brno artist, previously active in Olomouc. The way in which the artist approaches the spiritual movement of the figures, the non-dramatic gestures, the soft relief shapes and the spatial concept of the sculpture, enhance the effect of an epic scene. The sculptor’s oeuvre includes many altarpieces in Brno and its surroundings, typified by a spectacular form derived from Italian (Bernini) and Viennese (Donner) sculpture. The artist’s stucco work was particularly influenced by B. Fontana.
15bbc895-ece1-5072-8a0d-58528b3db808.location: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno
15bbc895-ece1-5072-8a0d-58528b3db808.artist: Jan Jiří Schauberger (? before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)

16315802-18c2-5330-ba73-5cd3cfe77f4a.name: *St. Joseph with Jesus and St. John the Baptist*
16315802-18c2-5330-ba73-5cd3cfe77f4a.description: In Croatia and especially in the north, there are a large number of works of the Slovene painter, Valentin Metzinger. An eclectic and accomplished painter, he was inspired by the works of the Bolognese artists Annibale Carracci and Guido Reni, and the paintings of the Venetian Mannerists. From the time of Metzinger’s arrival in Ljubljana in 1727, up to his death in 1759, his name and his works became the trademark of a large number of religious interiors throughout Slovenia and Croatia, particularly within Franciscan churches.

18d8c264-d9de-5469-85bc-d0bbaeb6448b.name: *Abraham’s Sacrifice of Isaac* (detail of an angel and Abraham)
18d8c264-d9de-5469-85bc-d0bbaeb6448b.description: Depicting the dramatic peak of the Old Testament story, an angel catches hold of the raised arm of Abraham, stopping him a moment before the sacrifice of his own son Isaac, the crouching figure of whom is on the ready-prepared pyre.
18d8c264-d9de-5469-85bc-d0bbaeb6448b.location: Altar of the Holy Cross (Church of the Holy Cross)

1d7a5af5-3037-5bd4-8ab2-a42543f3c28c.name: Revelation of St. Joseph Calasanctius
1d7a5af5-3037-5bd4-8ab2-a42543f3c28c.description: The side altarpiece represents the founder of the Piarist order, with his students, worshipping the Virgin Mary. The subject is associated with teaching, one of the chief objectives of the order. The picture complements the *Allegory of Education* by W. Träger.
1d7a5af5-3037-5bd4-8ab2-a42543f3c28c.location: Piarist Church of St. John the Baptist
1d7a5af5-3037-5bd4-8ab2-a42543f3c28c.artist: Josef Stern (1716 Graz – 1775 Brno), Wolfgang Träger (1714 Pilsen – 1763 Olomouc)

261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.name: Library
261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.description: The library equipment was enabled by a generous donation from Baron Trenck who is mummified in the monastery crypt. The ceiling painting represents John Bonaventura showing a crucifix to Thomas Aquinas in response to a query as to the origin of the sources of his writings. One remarkable item is a human skeleton in a display case amidst the other library cases. The skeleton was used for anatomy studies and also symbolised, within the library iconography, a *memento mori*.
261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno
261d6cf2-f4d5-5ea8-a4c4-7c1fe310d8d9.artist: Josef Stern (1716 Graz – 1775 Brno), Ondřej Schweigl (1735–1812 Brno)

2c0658b1-af70-5e4f-a9aa-8724f6488ff4.name: *St Mary of Help*
2c0658b1-af70-5e4f-a9aa-8724f6488ff4.description: The central image – after the well-known “miraculous” icon by Lucas Cranach the Elder – is “carried” by angels over a representation of 18th-century Osijek.

32a8ad1d-7f6d-50f5-86ce-2904db9b8e81.name: Façade
32a8ad1d-7f6d-50f5-86ce-2904db9b8e81.description: The façade, whose towers, gables and escutcheons were first completed in 1900, i.e. supplemented, most clearly show the influence of the Salzburg Dome. The exterior is maintained in the strict arrangement typical of South German Early Baroque. The towers and the centre of the façade form a unit. The two portal arches, separated by double pilasters (cf. St. Michael’s Church, Munich) already anticipate the configuration of the interior nave walls.

32b1e458-9669-5b2a-91d1-0cb33372a953.name: The lateral altars of the Chapterhouse
32b1e458-9669-5b2a-91d1-0cb33372a953.description: These were perhaps, originally, part of the main chapel and sacristy until the reign of King João III (1521–1557). The two lateral altars were installed during the reigns of King João V (r.1706–1750) and King José I (r.1750–1777). One is dedicated to the Death of Christ the other to Our Lady of Good Death.
32b1e458-9669-5b2a-91d1-0cb33372a953.location: Connected to the nave of the church

37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.name: Paintings and *azulejos* of the nave and main chapel
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.description:
The 20 ceiling paintings depicting the Life of the Virgin are by the Marcos da Cruz workshop. The walls are adorned with paintings by Bento Coelho da Silveira. They depict the Life of St. Claire (upper register) and the Life of St. Francis (lower register). Paintings by André Gonçalves decorate the triumphal arch. These feature the Coronation of the Virgin by the Holy Trinity. Paintings of St. Claire and St. Francis flank the archway. The nave *azulejos* are by the Dutch artist, Willem van der Kloet; they were commissioned in Holland. Close to the *rocaille* pulpit are *azulejos* featuring Franciscan monks praying. The *azulejos* in the main chapel are by Jan van Oort.  
These depict the vision of Pope Nicholas V when standing by the body of St. Francis.
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.dates: Ceiling paintings: c.1675–1690; triumphal arch paintings: c.1740–50; *azulejos*: 1698–1707; pulpit: 1747–1759; main altar: after 1755
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.location: Nave and main chapel, Church and Convent of Madre de Deus
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.artist: Painters: Marcos da Cruz [n.d.], Bento Coelho da Silveira (1648–1708), André Gonçalves (1685–1762); tile painters: Jan van Oort [n.d.], Willem van der Kloet [n.d.], Gabriel del Barco (1649–c.1703); woodcarver: Félix Adauto da Cunha (1649–c.1703)

3833a71f-0ae4-54fa-a584-49250b36be5a.name: High Altar of St. Catherine of Alexandria
3833a71f-0ae4-54fa-a584-49250b36be5a.description: The illusionist fresco St. Catherine Among Alexandrine philosophers and Writers is a quality *trompe l'oeil* painting displaying illusionist architecture of the Alexandrian temple with the huge figures of St. Catherine and her collocutors occupying the central part of the composition. The painted space spreads towards the background in almost accurate central perspective. On the sides, just above eye level, are St. Paul on the left and St. Peter on the right, while the attic is dedicated to the Holy Trinity accompanied by angels.
3833a71f-0ae4-54fa-a584-49250b36be5a.location: The sanctuary, eastern wall, Academy Church of St. Catherine

3872b95b-f605-5d55-a762-172880091112.name: The Good Government of Urban VIII
3872b95b-f605-5d55-a762-172880091112.description: The Good Government of Urban VIII, with Dignity in the centre flanked on the left by Prudence and on the right by the Delegated Power which receives a letter and is preparing to leave on a mission; on the left, the Forge of Vulcan, and on the right Peace and Fame.

3a82940b-0422-54ce-94e9-7b0610d5dd16.name: Cupola
3a82940b-0422-54ce-94e9-7b0610d5dd16.description: This was the first cupola built in Portugal, similar to that of St. Peter’s in Rome. Sixty-two metres high, it is marble outside and with polychrome marble inside. The cupola has an eight-sided form and eight windows, above which are the sculpted litanies of the Virgin Mary. Forty-one men worked simultaneously on the decoration “very well and at ease”, according to a testimony in contemporary sources.

3c4ef2fa-2d0c-53ea-a254-7f42269d568c.name: Sculpture of the Crucifixion
3c4ef2fa-2d0c-53ea-a254-7f42269d568c.description: The monumental bronze sculpture of the Crucifixion once belonged to the former Altar of the Holy Cross, where the mass for the people was read. Thematically, it completes the life-story of Christ narrated in the other altars. The Virgin Mary and John the Evangelist standing beside the cross, as well as Mary Magdalena kneeling at its foot, are shown in lamentation expressed through gestures of grief.
3c4ef2fa-2d0c-53ea-a254-7f42269d568c.location: In front of the choir / behind the modern altar

4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.name: Altar and choir
4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.description: The choir, oriented to the west, was renewed in 1730 in the contemporary Rococo style. On the occasion of the centennial of the Peace of 1648 a new gallery for the organ was installed. The slightly curved stucco is captivating in its simple elegance, its colour highlighting the choir. Although the gallery continues in the choir, the coloured Regency and Rococo stucco establishes a discrete, almost scenographic quality. The fresco on the ceiling shows the three theological virtues: Faith, Hope and Charity. Around the altar, as at the pulpit, paintings depict scenes from the Life of Christ: the Baptism, Resurrection, Pentecost and Last Supper. The two most important ritualistic elements in the church – altar and pulpit – together harmonise in form and content, dedicated fully to the teachings of Christ.
4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.dates: c. 1653: retable; 1673/74: paintings; 1730: organ and decoration of the vault; 1748: renovation of the gallery and organ; 1767: altar
4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.artist: Johann Heiss (1640–1704), Johann Ulrich Mayr (1630–1704), Johannes Spillenberger (1628–1679), Josef Werner (1637–1710); Johann Georg Bergmüller (1688–1762); Johann Esaias Nilson (active 1721–1728); Ignaz Wilhelm Verhelst (1729–1792)

4721206d-edec-5f4f-8475-830cfd0d5bb0.name: Crucifix
4721206d-edec-5f4f-8475-830cfd0d5bb0.description: The cross, created by the sculptor of Stams Monastery, Andreas Thamasch in the year of his death, is a “wound” or “Blutheilands” crucifix and is also referred to as a “Plague Cross”. With his last work Thamasch succeeded in creating an especially expressive example of this type; the stirring face wracked with torment, the body covered with wounds.

49f2b9ac-02d2-5d5a-b795-331d46920de1.name: Altar of St. Cajetan
49f2b9ac-02d2-5d5a-b795-331d46920de1.description: The altar bears a masterpiece of German Baroque painting dedicated to the founder of the Theatine order.

4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.name: Pulpit
4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.description: The pulpit, decorated in slender *rocailles*, is positioned prominently within the church *vis-à-vis* the gallery according to its role in the Lutheran rite. A life-size wooden crucifix above the pulpit and two paintings of Christ’s Passion by Johann Heinrich Schönfeld at either side complete the Christological ensemble.
4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.location: Wall on the right-hand side, Evangelical Lutheran Church of the Holy Cross
4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.artist: Johann Esaias Nilson (1721–1728); Ignaz Wilhelm Verhelst (1729–1792); Johann Heinrich Schönfeld (1609–1684)

4ad97887-f621-598c-8c7f-52693a816738.name: St. Felix of Cantalice
4ad97887-f621-598c-8c7f-52693a816738.description: The entrance of the church, in sloping terrain, was adjusted by a terrace with statues of Capuchin saints. The sculptor, who trained in the Rhine Basin region, worked in the Brno workshop of J. J. Schauberger. His compact figures are noteworthy for their expressive faces.
4ad97887-f621-598c-8c7f-52693a816738.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno

4b86710e-568a-5cec-95d8-65d5bb9609bd.name: Sacristy (general view)
4b86710e-568a-5cec-95d8-65d5bb9609bd.description: The sacristy owns what can be considered a complete and unique – both in terms of iconography and style – series of *rocaille* wood-carved and Baroque sculptures, and also a series of Benedictine figures.
4b86710e-568a-5cec-95d8-65d5bb9609bd.artist: Friar José Cipriano da Cruz Sousa (c. 1645–1716) and others

5189e709-985a-5612-9c80-28cf963cf0c0.name: *Christ*
5189e709-985a-5612-9c80-28cf963cf0c0.description: With a prominent diagonal axes, both groups at the ends of the altar direct the viewer’s gaze towards the central motif – the redemptive sacrifice of the Crucified Christ. Carved in white marble, yellow marble frames the figure of the dying Christ. Additional emphasis is achieved by a pair of volutes that edge the upper part of the frame and stand out against a background of black marble drapery, the folds of which are arranged in rays.

52383801-0cd8-5000-8d48-ffc62ed390a0.name: *St Michael Overthrows the Fallen Angels and the Coronation of Mary the Virgin*
52383801-0cd8-5000-8d48-ffc62ed390a0.description: As counter-reformatory Catholic propaganda linked to the iconography of the Jesuit church St Michael in Munich, the main fresco addresses the victorious battle of the Archangel Michael against the apostate angels, who blatantly  represent Protestantism. Crowned by the Trinity, Mary, as the Queen of Angels, oversees the happenings that are surrounded by Marian Symbols.

53f0ae70-9e34-55bc-bbcb-4ee9c86e09a0.name: Stucco
53f0ae70-9e34-55bc-bbcb-4ee9c86e09a0.description: The stuccowork, executed during 1634–7, is the work of Georg Braun of the Wessobrun school according to designs from Hans Schor and Florian Nut. Panels, vases, festoons, and draperies, framed by rod motifs, underscore the structural elements in emulation of the austere panelled stucco of the South German (Munich) style. The transept and choir also contain ornaments in the emerging scrollwork style, designed c. 1640/50 by Oswald Kaiser.
53f0ae70-9e34-55bc-bbcb-4ee9c86e09a0.artist: Georg Braun [n.d.], Hans Schor (1585–1674), Florian Nut [n.d.], Frair Oswald Kaiser [n.d.]

58db5d91-9a5a-5cc7-993f-9e9b4c91e765.name: Inscription on the entrance doorway
58db5d91-9a5a-5cc7-993f-9e9b4c91e765.description: The detail shows the inscription above the entrance to the Chapel of Bones. It addresses those who enter the chapel, reminding them of the folly of vanity and concentration on mundane affairs, which must give way to an exemplary life and to the denial of earthly belongings. The inscription reads: “*Nós ossos que aqui estamos pelos vossos esperamos*” (“We bones lying here are waiting to be joined by yours”).

58fa3a97-2ab3-5a6d-aeef-3f7f461c21ff.name: The Triumph of Peace and Justice
58fa3a97-2ab3-5a6d-aeef-3f7f461c21ff.description: The Triumph of Peace and Justice, with the flying figures of Justice, holding the fasces, and of Abundance, with the fruits.

59c51cf5-bbb6-53c6-b4c9-b11995b0abfd.name: Ulrich Altar
59c51cf5-bbb6-53c6-b4c9-b11995b0abfd.description: With its elegant Rococo shapes, the side altar, crafted by the great master of the local guild of sculptors at that time, is dedicated to St. Ulrich as the diocese patron and shows his apotheosis in the medium of sculpture.
59c51cf5-bbb6-53c6-b4c9-b11995b0abfd.location: Middle side chapel on the left

5c94a693-94d2-5ebe-82b9-608c53f0f3fd.name: High altar
5c94a693-94d2-5ebe-82b9-608c53f0f3fd.description: The imposing high altar with six columns above a concave ground plan was altered considerably in the late 19th century and subsequently returned to its original form during restoration work concluded in 1982. The original altarpiece, the *Assumption of Mary* painted by Franz Laukas in 1724, was also reinserted. The two masterfully executed statues of St. Joseph and Joachim, the work of Andreas Köll (c. 1720) were also repainted white.

5d883aff-c791-5728-975f-c3f848744787.name: Upper Synagogue
5d883aff-c791-5728-975f-c3f848744787.description: Form the 15th century onwards, part of the area below the chateau became a cultural and spiritual centre for the Moravian Jewish community. There was a Talmudic school, 12 synagogues and other places of worship. In the second half of the 16th century the legendary Rabbi Löw, allegedly the creator of the Prague golem, worked there. After a fire, the buildings and the synagogue were restored by master builders of the court. The synagogue is the only extant example of a “Polish-style” temple in Czech lands. It features four cupolas supported by four columns standing in the centre of a hall. The adjacent Jewish cemetery is among the largest and oldest in the Czech Republic.

60118261-bf39-5b51-becf-89deec2d3d9c.name: Invention of the Holy Cross
60118261-bf39-5b51-becf-89deec2d3d9c.description: The Counter-Reformation activities of the Capuchin order are reflected in this sizeable picture for the high altar. It depicts a key scene in the legend of the Invention of the Holy Cross on which Christ was crucified, showing Empress Helen, the mother of Constantine the Great, as she witnesses the Cross's authenticity; that the touch of the cross brings a dead youth back to life and cures a terminally-ill woman. Behind the empress stands Bishop Makarios. The use of light within the picture makes much of the resurrection, while the rhetorical gestures, artistic rendering of richly varied surfaces and a monumental compositional structure, make for an impressive painting. The canvas, considered the first Baroque painting in Moravia, originated at the same time as the *Crucifixion* Sandrart painted for the Cathedral of St. Stephen in Vienna, which was said to have been commissioned by Count Václav Eusebius of Lobkowitz, one of the most powerful men in the Viennese imperial court.
60118261-bf39-5b51-becf-89deec2d3d9c.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross

607f2261-ddcf-5352-a0ee-33f57d581ee2.name: Cemetery Cloister
607f2261-ddcf-5352-a0ee-33f57d581ee2.description: The Monastery includes two cloisters: the Refectory Cloister ruins; the Cemetery Cloister, in the classical style, comprises arched galleries richly decorated with tiles that are incomplete. The monastic areas or adjoining wings include the Jericho Garden; the Courtyard of St. John in its original state as far as its structure and design are concerned, and complete with a small garden and monumental fountain at the centre and the Wine Cellar Courtyard.

6170eca7-efbd-5cb1-8474-f0ef9b1c591c.name: Carillons
6170eca7-efbd-5cb1-8474-f0ef9b1c591c.description: A Flanders-made ensemble of two carillons with 92 bells commissioned by King D. João V, representing the world’s largest historical set. The north tower carillon has 45 bells and the south tower carillon 47 bells. The bells are made of bronze and their total weight is 217 tons. According to tradition, when the king was told the astronomic price of only one carillon, he answered "I didn't expect it to be that cheap, I'll have two."

632ade3d-0ea4-5615-a757-c3571c4ba4b4.name: Pulpit
632ade3d-0ea4-5615-a757-c3571c4ba4b4.description: One of the most important sculptural centres in Adriatic Croatia during the 18th century, Rijeka boasted Baroque churches that today form a thesaurus of Baroque sculpture of both known and anonymous masters. Between 1733 and 1772 Antonio Michelazzi’s sculpture workshop in Rijeka employed many altar makers and sculptors from Friuli and Gorica. This pulpit – with the seated figures of the four evangelists Matthew, Mark, Luke and John and bearing Christ’s monogram on the concave front – is supported by two massive volutes. It represents a strong plastic accent in the church since all the other altarpieces are within the radial chapels.

65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.name: Ceiling fresco: *The Veneration of St. Charles Borromeo*
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.description: The frescos in Volders are among the most important of Knoller’s works. The apotheosis of the church patron in the main cupola is the high point of the programme, surrounded by scenes from his life. As an important representative of the Counter Reformation his veneration goes hand in hand with the victory of Catholicism. Knoller’s clear composition with monumental figures already contains elements of Classicism.
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.location: Main cupola, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

6b1e3b8c-0d8c-5527-b9d3-642e4b7b458f.name: Bethlehem Chapel
6b1e3b8c-0d8c-5527-b9d3-642e4b7b458f.description: The Burial Chapel of the Virgin Mary is followed by a two-storey building loosely designed after Christ’s tomb in Jerusalem. On the ground floor are marble reliefs of the Birth of Christ, the Adoration of the Magi and the Flight into Egypt; on the first floor there is a chapel featuring Mary Magdalene and the corpse of Christ.
6b1e3b8c-0d8c-5527-b9d3-642e4b7b458f.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka

6b44fe59-7a74-52bd-b3df-12c9adba8bba.name: *St Michael the Archangel and the Battle for the Liberation of Osijek from the Turks*
6b44fe59-7a74-52bd-b3df-12c9adba8bba.description: The compositional structure of the painting skilfully combines two themes: the *Fall of the Angel* in the upper part, and a depiction of the battle for the liberation of Osijek from the Turks, in the lower part. The traditional apocalyptic scene with fallen angels lying beneath the feet of the archangel – the victor – is replaced in this rendition by a depiction of the liberation of Osijek from the Turks. The artist based the symbolism of the victory of Good over Evil – of the archangel over Lucifer – with the victory of the Catholic Church over Islam. This was entirely appropriate for the environment intended, for Osijek had been under Turkish siege for 160 years (1526–1687).
6b44fe59-7a74-52bd-b3df-12c9adba8bba.location: High Altar, Parish Church of St. Michael

6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.name: Façade
6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.description: The entire idiosyncrasy and fancy of the Early Baroque building can be best seen on the façade which appears as if it was pieced together from a construction kit composed of the most bizarre forms. The departure from the classical theory of form shows that the dilettante architect (= enthusiast) was still an adherent of Mannerism, drawing his vocabulary of forms from religious tracts. Little of the often classical austerity of German Early Baroque is in evidence here. The chapels at the sides of the façade were added later in accordance with the existing design.

6d5d6c37-c76c-5c00-aa84-68da154b6726.name: Burial Chapel of St. Ulrich
6d5d6c37-c76c-5c00-aa84-68da154b6726.description: The decoration of the crypt, dedicated to the patron saint of the diocese St. Ulrich, is a prime example for the local variant of the Rococo style in Augsburg, characterised through its playfulness and ornamental abundance. By contrast, the sarcophagus with the figure of the saint stands fully within the tradition of Baroque sepulchre culture.

6f69a47e-294c-59c1-8a2b-a6157999fccc.name: Pulpit
6f69a47e-294c-59c1-8a2b-a6157999fccc.description: The richly decorated pulpit in the scrollwork style, donated by Claudia de’ Medici c. 1640 (monogram “C” with crown), is attributed to the Jesuit Friar Oswald Kaiser.

7212b05e-72ab-5a3f-96b6-a69fb2c79452.name: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno
7212b05e-72ab-5a3f-96b6-a69fb2c79452.description: The vault of the single-nave building opens onto a celestial sphere with a monumental fresco and scenes from the lives of the Saints John and Loreto. The illusionary architecture graduates into genuine pilasters and stucco decoration. The main section depicts the Birth of St. John the Baptist, while the presbytery vault, separated by a “triumphal arch”, features the signs in the sky described in the Revelation of St. John.
7212b05e-72ab-5a3f-96b6-a69fb2c79452.location: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno

74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.name: Chapel of St. John the Baptist
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.description: The Chapel of St. John the Baptist, with its lavishly ornamented surfaces in coloured marble and other stone facings, is in the Roman Baroque style. The bronze gates of the front balustrade and the bronze side doors display the monogram of King João V. The side panels – the Annunciation (right) and Pentecost (left) – and the central panel – The Baptism of Christ – as well as the floor (displaying an armillary sphere), are mosaics. Several types of ornamental stone are used in the chapel. An important collection of liturgical objects was produced as part of the interior decoration project: gold-embroidered vestments, several metal objects – candleholders, reliquaries and crucifixes – and also books for the Mass.
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.dates: The interior decoration of the chapel was commissioned from Rome in 1740 by King João V (1706–50) and constructed between 1742 and 1750, when it was officially inaugurated in Lisbon.
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.location: Church Interior, Church of São Roque
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.artist: In Rome architects Luigi Vanvitelli (1700–1773) and Niccolò Salvi (1697–1751) directed hundreds of artists and craftsmen; Mosaic: Agostino Masucci (1691–1758) and Mattia Moretti (d. 1779); Floor mosaic: Enrico Enuo.

74d429db-0e98-5a57-908f-8cf2399a89f7.name: Loreto and the so-called Náchod Chapel (St Anna church)
74d429db-0e98-5a57-908f-8cf2399a89f7.description: The Cardinal had a pilgrimage chapel built within the Capuchin Monastery in 1622. The chapel, modelled on an Italian Loreto to symbolise the Holy stable, the birthplace of Christ, was the first of its kind in Czech lands. In 1636 the Church of St. Anne was constructed next to the chapel, with a statue of the Black Madonna the scourge of the heretics. The complex was richly decorated with statues and stuccos. The church and the Loreto were destroyed by fire; only the chancel and the Náchod Chapel survive.

792acd8a-ec3d-58f9-aac4-9e904aebd7b3.name: Altar of St. Ignatius
792acd8a-ec3d-58f9-aac4-9e904aebd7b3.description: Archbishop Emerik Esterhazy was the donor for the marble Altar of St. Ignatius. In its architectural structure, the altarpiece belongs to a type designed for jesuit churches by Andrea Pozzo. The two side sculptures represent the two Jesuit saints, St. Frances Regis and St. Frances Xavier.
792acd8a-ec3d-58f9-aac4-9e904aebd7b3.location: The first side chapel of St. Ignatius on the left-hand (north) side of the nave

7bb44db4-3bdf-59d8-a571-b142ef6d20a2.name: Lamentation of Christ
7bb44db4-3bdf-59d8-a571-b142ef6d20a2.description: The affecting  painting with Ettal Monastery as provenance is related to the Roman influenced classicism of Knoller’s academic colleague, Anton Raphael Mengs (1728–79), and is thus compositionally close to corresponding depictions from Annibale Caracci (1560–1609).
7bb44db4-3bdf-59d8-a571-b142ef6d20a2.location: Altar of the middle side chapel on the right

8277ff67-ae58-5300-9fc6-c53e66fabfca.name: Stairway
8277ff67-ae58-5300-9fc6-c53e66fabfca.description: The Tibães Stairway was built almost simultaneously with the first phase of construction of Bom Jesus de Braga in around 1725. It can be considered as part of the baroque “fashion” of stairways.

82817bab-a50a-5ce1-8f65-0d7b359e74ee.name: Chapel of St. John Nepomuk (Sacrament Chapel)
82817bab-a50a-5ce1-8f65-0d7b359e74ee.description: The chapel of the popular patron saint of Bavaria, St. John Nepomuk (today, known as the Sacrament Chapel) was designed in 1737/38 by Egid Quirin Asam. The dynamically curved architecture and the ecstatic sculptures of the patron and his namesakes, John the Baptist and the Evangelist, refer clearly to designs of the Roman High Baroque.

83c8fa85-4413-5d4d-90af-066b8e8a993e.name: The Stigmatisation of St. Francis
83c8fa85-4413-5d4d-90af-066b8e8a993e.description: Rotter, who specialised in altarpieces, easel paintings, frescos and decorative wall paintings, was a major figure within the Brno guild of painters. His oeuvre is known from the 1740s, when he worked for the Augustinians and Premonstratensians in Hradisko near Olomouc, although the frescos are not preserved. The side-altar picture comes from Rotter’s late phase, when he embraced closed shapes and more simple colour schemes.
83c8fa85-4413-5d4d-90af-066b8e8a993e.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno

89c05fc9-f779-5631-bd7e-77ed9cf6185a.name: Altarpiece: *Baptism of the Indian Nobleman* and *St. Francis Xavier’s Miracle of the Crab*
89c05fc9-f779-5631-bd7e-77ed9cf6185a.description: The altarpieces of the side chapel dedicated to St. Francis Xavier, glorify him as the most important missionary of the Jesuit order, who, like Ignatius, was conferred sainthood in 1622. The painting depicting the baptism of the Indian nobleman is attributed to Johann Heinrich Schönfeld, together with the scene on the rear wall of the miracle of the crab in which Francis Xavier received his crucifix back from the sea. The images refer to the Jesuit order as the main bearer of the missionary counter-reformation.
89c05fc9-f779-5631-bd7e-77ed9cf6185a.location: First right-hand side chapel, Jesuit Church Innsbruck

8efd1f12-5052-51ee-9e54-57876db45757.name: Chapel of All Saints
8efd1f12-5052-51ee-9e54-57876db45757.description: Under a stuccoed baldachin, lifted by angels, the altar of relics is presented to the believers. To its sides, the skeletons of the Four Holy Abbots: Wigpertus, Nidgarius, Adalbero and Thosse are presented in showcases. The connection of their dead bodies with an image of the Crucifixion suggests their successful emulation of Christ.
8efd1f12-5052-51ee-9e54-57876db45757.artist: Matthias Lotter [n.d.]; Johann Georg Knappich (1637–1704); Johann Georg Schmierer [n.d.]

92a08715-2350-530f-b788-77727a9408e0.name: Sculptures of the chancel screen
92a08715-2350-530f-b788-77727a9408e0.description: Towards the end of World War II the entire choir area was destroyed by fire, including the high altar, the choir screen and the tabernacle. Of the four evangelist figures flanking the passageways through to the choir, only Marcus, John and Lucas have remained intact. They are counted among the most accomplished Baroque sculptures in Bavaria.

9457f0e4-3fcf-50a6-aec1-b755319d7119.name: Ground-plan reconstruction
9457f0e4-3fcf-50a6-aec1-b755319d7119.description: The original ground plan was altered by the construction of the sacristy and oratory. The symbolic design of a four-apse central construction is an allusion on the “double” temple in Jerusalem, close to the Holy Grave.
9457f0e4-3fcf-50a6-aec1-b755319d7119.artist: František Benedikt Klíčník? (1677 Ivanovice na Hané – 1755 Brno)

9472b01a-4d61-5273-a492-4252a74c1f5d.name: Souls in Purgatory
9472b01a-4d61-5273-a492-4252a74c1f5d.description: The altarpieces originated in parallel with the wall paintings. Leicher had studied in a Piarist school in Příbor, and worked for the order in Mikulov. He probably mediated commissions in Mikulov and Kroměříž to his friend, F. A. Maulbertsch with whom he collaborated, and whose specific style became the cornerstone of his work. The dramatic air of the predella picture derives from its subject. Leicher, influenced by M. Unterberger rather than the expressivity of P. Troger, usually opted for a more classical, lyrical approach.

948b8793-f65d-5074-831e-9d04a6833408.name: Holy Stairs
948b8793-f65d-5074-831e-9d04a6833408.description: A three-shouldered staircase is the conceptual climax of the Loreto Chapel. Praying on their knees, worshippers ascend to an Ecce Homo group, stopping at the symbols of Christ’s suffering. The 28 steps recall the stairs climbed by Christ in the Palace of Jerusalem after his condemnation by Pontius Pilate. The entrance portal of the Loreto stable is guarded by a pair of angels, and a relief of the Transfer of Santa Casa (Holy House) with the Virgin Mary at the centre, surrounded by the patron saints of the church. The vaults of the gallery around the Holy House and above the stairs, placed in front of the presbytery, were painted by F. Ř. I. Eckstein, and feature scenes from the Life of the Virgin Mary. They are framed by illusionary architecture graduating into grisaille paintings, also covering the Holy House. The chapel contains a number of pictures by Brno artists, among whom, J. I. Havelka, who created a great number of paintings for the Minorite order and probably lived in the monastery.
948b8793-f65d-5074-831e-9d04a6833408.location: Minorite Church of the Saints John and Loreto
948b8793-f65d-5074-831e-9d04a6833408.artist: Mořic Grimm (1669 Achdorf – 1757 Brno), Anton Johann Ospel

949beb48-45b8-5856-b363-32eb9f163579.name: Frescos of the *Virtues of St. Corbinian*; the *Apotheosis of St. Corbinian*; *Theological Virtues*; the *Enthroned Mother of God*; *Adoration of the Lamb*
949beb48-45b8-5856-b363-32eb9f163579.description: The Asam's paintings and stucco form an inseparable symbiosis; even the frescos participate in a decorative system, unfolding in front of a painted ground of brocade. The impetus to unite the genres becomes most apparent in the painted *trompe l'oeil* cupola, following the style of Roman examples (S. Ignazio and Il Gesù). While the high altar is dedicated to the Virgin Mary, the ceiling represents the second patron, St. Corbinian. The frescos show (starting in the west): the *Virtues of St. Corbinian Annihilating the Vice* and *The apotheosis of St. Corbinian*; followed by: *Theological Virtues*, framed by the coat-of-arms of the bishops of Freising; *The Enthroned Mother of God* (in the *trompe l´oeil* cupola); and the *Adoration of the lamb*.
949beb48-45b8-5856-b363-32eb9f163579.artist: Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750); Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739)

94e616f1-2015-5f83-a8bb-76438726f9d0.name: *Souls in Purgatory*
94e616f1-2015-5f83-a8bb-76438726f9d0.description: The dynamic contour lines and the sharp edges stress the drama of the scene: souls in the flames of purgatory, and hovering above them, the redemptive figure of an angel.

95109161-87b5-5953-88a1-413967eb4236.name: Ceiling Painting
95109161-87b5-5953-88a1-413967eb4236.description: The original ceiling painting comprising architectural elements was made by the Spanish painter Francisco Venegas at the end of the 16th century. The Triumph of the Holy Cross, among other scenes from the bible, were mostly inspired by engravings from Antwerp and added in the early 17th century by the Portuguese painter, Amaro do Vale.

962e003b-defe-58d1-85ea-6105adc77f5a.name: *St. Charles Borromeo* (detail)
962e003b-defe-58d1-85ea-6105adc77f5a.location: Upper inner rim of the monument

9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.name: View from the east
9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.description: Although the arrangement of the rest of the building is not as closely crowded as the façade, the walls are still un-classical in their configuration. The superstructure with perimeter pilasters throughout and an attic zone is modelled on St. Peter’s in Rome, as is the building’s basic design with domed tri-conch. The tower, expressing the motif of the Trinity, was originally designed with a spiral-shaped pinnacle.

97fe6083-dbd1-5242-b2e0-5e77a101a930.name: Eternal light
97fe6083-dbd1-5242-b2e0-5e77a101a930.description: Reliefs in gilded copper represent St. John the Baptist, St. John the Evangelist, St. Francis of Assisi, and others. The lamp’s summit consists of the Holy Trinity and the Virgin Immaculata, patron saint of the Minorites. The eternal light is usually hung in front of the high altar as a symbol of the Lord’s presence.
97fe6083-dbd1-5242-b2e0-5e77a101a930.location: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno

9907ee8c-c9bc-5075-a64d-986d4821b30a.name: Vault with stucco and ceiling paintings
9907ee8c-c9bc-5075-a64d-986d4821b30a.description: The ceiling frescos, framed by delicate strapwork stucco, were painted by Franz Laukas from Prutz. The five large panels depict scenes from the life of Mary, accompanied by eight smaller Mariological pictures and six scenes depicting the legend of the pilgrimage. Laukas’s painting style displays a clear folk art element – in particular the smaller panels with their charming naivety reminiscent of votive painting.
9907ee8c-c9bc-5075-a64d-986d4821b30a.artist: Franz Laukas (1690–1765); Anton Gigl (1700–1769), Augustin Gigl (dates unknown, active in the first half of the 18th century)

9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.name: Chapel of Our Lady of the Doctrine
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.description: The main image of this chapel represents Our Lady of the Doctrine (St. Ann with the Virgin Mary in her arms). Although the chapel was built in the 17th century, the decoration is typical of the Portuguese Baroque “National style”, which developed during the late 17th and early 18th century. This side chapel is the only one where gilded woodwork covers the whole of the interior surface including the barrel-vaulted ceiling.
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.dates: Work on the chapel began on 1 April 1634 and it was used by the Brotherhood of Our Lady of the Doctrine as their headquarters. The stonework was finally completed in 1690.
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.location: Church Interior, Church of São Roque
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.artist: The woodwork is by José Rodrigues Ramalho (1660–1721) according to a contract dated 1688 between him and the Brotherhood. The stonework was executed by master masons, Manuel Antunes and João Teixeira, whose exact dates are unknown.

9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.name: Chapel of Our Lady of Piety
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.description: The design for the retable is centred on a representation of Calvary. A 17th-century sculpture of the Pietà completes the tribune. The wood carving is exuberantly multi-coloured as a result of the variety of gold leaf that covers it.
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.dates: The construction and decoration was overseen by the Brotherhood of Our Lady of Piety. According to an inscription, work began in September 1686 and was completed by 1711. The retable dates from 1708. The gilding was added in 1716.
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.location: Church Interior, Church of São Roque
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.artist: The retable was made by the 18th-century master carver Bento da Fonseca de Azevedo

9e276d65-268c-5885-a7c1-1b671be8c8e8.name: View of the sanctuary
9e276d65-268c-5885-a7c1-1b671be8c8e8.description: The architect of the Church of St. Ignatius in Dubrovnik, Andrea Pozzo, envisaged a fresco painting for the sanctuary, dividing it with pillars into three parts – as he had done in his own painting in the church of the same name in Rome – and setting the iconographical programme. The programme was perceived as the *Apotheosis of the Work of St. Ignatius* in the central field of the sanctuary, the *Encounter of St. Ignatius with St. Francis Xavier and St. Francis Borgia* in the side fields and *St. Ignatius in Heavenly Glory* on the ceiling of the sanctuary. The wall paintings were executed by the Sicilian painter of Spanish descent (who trained in Rome and Naples), Gaetano Garcia. Looking to show case patterns from Rome, like Pozzo's St. Ignatius and the Church of St. Agnese in Agone (with dome frescos painted by Carlo Ferri), Garcia achieved an impressive High Baroque composition, with a pronounced dynamic, opulent colouring and an effective play of light and shadow. The largest Baroque fresco cycle in Dalmatia, it gives some inkling of the splendour intended for the interior of the Dubrovnik Jesuit church, had the painting programme – which probably included the ceiling of the nave – been carried out to the end.
9e276d65-268c-5885-a7c1-1b671be8c8e8.location: Walls and ceiling of the sanctuary, Jesuit Church of St Ignatius

a95515d5-18b6-558f-b87d-d9d3eeff31fe.name: *The Bronze Serpent*
a95515d5-18b6-558f-b87d-d9d3eeff31fe.description: An Old Testament scene of powerful dramatic charge, the dynamically composed sculptural group is organised around a diagonal line. The ornamental articulation of the drapery of Moses’ cloak is a recognisable feature of Robba’s stylistic language.
a95515d5-18b6-558f-b87d-d9d3eeff31fe.location: Altar of the Holy Cross (Church of the Holy Cross)

aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.name: Altar of St. Dionisius (Altar of the Holy Martyrs)
aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.description: The Altar of St. Dionisius combines sculptures by the early Baroque sculptor from Varasdin, Ivan Jakob Altenbach, and paintings by the Slovenina painter, Hans Georg Geiger. The first domestic sculptor of major artistic note, Ivan Jakob Altenbach appeared in the mid-1670s. His work shows essentially that he overcame the surviving forms of Mannerism to achieve the stylistic features of the Baroque. The Jesuit church in Leoben, Styria, influenced the conservative, two-storey structure of the wooden retable.
aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.location: The side chapel of St. Martyrs (St. Dionisius) on the right-hand (south) side of the nave
aaa73ab6-82bc-549b-89fe-7ef1622228fa.artist: Ivan Jakob Altenbach (active c. 1675–d. before 1692), Hans Georg Geiger (active 1639–d. 1681)

aea13279-eedb-5f94-9955-da7b4271af44.name: The High Altar
aea13279-eedb-5f94-9955-da7b4271af44.description: Made of Carrara marble with polychrome incrustations, in its dimensions the high altar dominates the other six altars placed in six radial chapels. Extending towards the vault of the chapel with its high central attic “inhabited” with small angels and a central figure of the Holy Father surrounded by rounded clouds, its slanted side “wings” with side passages in the lower part, fills the whole of the sanctuary forming a concave. There is a central wooden Gothic crucifix and in the side-niches are sculptures of St. Vitus and St. Modest.

b1a77d33-eb7b-5b94-86ac-a5048091f551.name: *Transverberation of the Heart of St Teresa*
b1a77d33-eb7b-5b94-86ac-a5048091f551.description: The ecstasy or rapture of St. Theresa is represented here by use of intensive colour contrasts and dynamic light and shadow throughout the vertical composition. The cheerful atmosphere of the painting does not suit the mystical subject matter – the vision of St. Theresa, a Seraph driving the point of a lance through her heart repeatedly, causing her both spiritual and physical pain.

b3dc84c7-1930-5b07-b085-55d198c770fa.name: St. Vincent and St. Sebastian
b3dc84c7-1930-5b07-b085-55d198c770fa.description: Depicting the Martyrs St. Sebastian and St. Vincent, these sculptures represent just two pieces from The Royal Commission, which includes among other precious items 56 Italian sculptures, representing the most important collection of Italian Baroque sculpture outside Italy. The two sculptures illustrated here are made from marble; each one is 3.58-meters tall.

b7c0b98d-c15d-53e7-87ca-e9455c41bd5a.name: Choir and crossing
b7c0b98d-c15d-53e7-87ca-e9455c41bd5a.description: Located at the centre of the building is the crossing, above which rises an octagonal cupola. A special feature is formed by the transitional pendentives, which here are filled in as opposed to being concavely arched. The tambour, studded with large windows, has an eight-sided cloister vault above it. The choir, considerably lower than the cross-arms due to its apse, has been under reconstruction since 2004 as part of the work on the high altar (from 1757) which was destroyed in 1943. The original altarpiece has been replaced by a work from Antonio Balestra from the story of St. Jacob. The straight-sided choir is flanked by two choir lofts, supported by stucco angels.

b985235f-025a-5eed-a7b8-96646d281fd8.name: The Triumph of Religion and Spirituality
b985235f-025a-5eed-a7b8-96646d281fd8.description: The Triumph of Religion and Spirituality, where Science, holding a book on the one hand and fire on the other, gazes at the Heaven above, the true source of knowledge. Down next to her, Religion holding a tripod.

c18e8d6d-69e1-5154-b742-7142e553dfce.name: Stuccowork
c18e8d6d-69e1-5154-b742-7142e553dfce.description: Stucco floral ornamentation and figurative scenes depict the life of the patron saint and saints to which the side chapels were dedicated between 1713 and 1726. The stuccowork, by the Italian master Anton Joseph Quadrio, was constructed between 1713 and 1721, and an anonymous Italian master between 1724 and 1726. With this exquisite work, St. Catherine's reached the ideal of *bel composto*, the characteristic Baroque unity of architecture, sculpture and painting.

c1acfc20-ced7-5631-9eba-98e3d6d38ec3.name: Wall covered with bones
c1acfc20-ced7-5631-9eba-98e3d6d38ec3.description: The Baroque sensibility reinforces a tendency arising from the late Middle Ages, which makes death and even funerals a spectacle aimed at showing the deceased, as far as possible, cheered up until the final destination: his or her grave and eternal resting place. The concept of a *Boa Morte* “Gentle Death” is the point of the prayers to Nossa Senhora da Boa Morte, whose origins go back to this tradition.

c1efc606-bb1a-5e6b-a789-0a668d5179a7.name: Interior of the church
c1efc606-bb1a-5e6b-a789-0a668d5179a7.description: High Baroque longitudinal single-nave type with lateral chapels and dominant sanctuary

c7eaf695-c32d-5a9b-abe4-003a1cc59469.name: Column and vault with bones
c7eaf695-c32d-5a9b-abe4-003a1cc59469.description: A spectacular image of the shortness of Life and the inevitability of Death. The skull and bones are the earthly evidence of the Death of the Body, in opposition to the aesthetic Joy of Redemption or Salvation. This trend for exhibiting naked bones – so called *Morte Secca* (“Dry Death”) – encompasses the allegory of Christian meditation: “Life is just a short passage; this world is not the ultimate destiny; the final destiny is the salvation of the soul.”

c98afbe4-8f44-5607-bb49-a1a56098da61.name: Library
c98afbe4-8f44-5607-bb49-a1a56098da61.description: The entrance to the library, with a ceiling-painting of the 12-year-old Jesus in the temple disputing with the elders (the first example of Jesus’ preaching), opens with Prudence and Knowledge; Wisdom is painted on the door. The library, with its well-preserved furniture, is among the most significant Baroque libraries in Czech lands.

cc3aa5b9-a146-5ee6-b9a4-5560a9f85e69.name: Altar of the Virgin Mary (high altar)
cc3aa5b9-a146-5ee6-b9a4-5560a9f85e69.description: The high altar, designed by Hans Krumpper, is an early example of a combined retable and tabernacle – the latter manufactured on the explicit demand of the Prince-Bishop by Philipp Dirr. The Rubens’ altarpiece is a replica (the original has been conserved in Munich since 1927). It shows the “Madonna on the Crescent Moon” with the archangel Michael triumphant over evil, especially paganism.
cc3aa5b9-a146-5ee6-b9a4-5560a9f85e69.artist: Hans Krumpper (c. 1570–1634); Philipp Dirr (c. 1582–1633); Pieter Paul Rubens (1577–1640)

ce3e1a26-65b3-5643-a5eb-b18a3b8d53e4.name: Assumption of Mary
ce3e1a26-65b3-5643-a5eb-b18a3b8d53e4.description: Upon electoral request, the altarpiece of the once Early Baroque high altar depicts the Assumption of Mary according to the saint’s patronage of the church. The Munich painter portrayed himself as the apostle Johannes looking out of the painting. Theme and composition follow a copperplate depiction of the high altarpiece of Peter Paul Rubens in the Cathedral of Antwerp.

cfc8b095-24f6-594f-a08a-a320412bd52e.name: Interior of the church
cfc8b095-24f6-594f-a08a-a320412bd52e.description: The interior is a perfect blend of different arts and techniques. The colours of the frescoes harmonise perfectly with the white and gold stucco decorations and with the soft light coming from the windows.

d4c28ae8-32bb-5728-b823-2fbca193bbeb.name: The Tree-of-Jesse Monstrance
d4c28ae8-32bb-5728-b823-2fbca193bbeb.description: The masterpiece of a local goldsmith features busts within a 122cm tall arabesque depicting Christ's family tree growing from Jesse. Christ’s body is present as the consecrated host in an ostensory which is fitted in St Mary’s lap.

d6a6bbee-1004-5fe5-93a3-c845fe7b8380.name: Library
d6a6bbee-1004-5fe5-93a3-c845fe7b8380.description:
A significant Enlightenment Library with around 36,000 volumes amassed through royal commission. It has a cruciform layout with a multi-coloured limestone floor and Rocaille shelves.  
Some rare works furnish its shelves to this day: the *Nuremberg Chronicle* (1493) or the *Theatrvm Orbis Terrarvm* by Ortelius (1595) and a nucleus of scores from musicians such as João de Sousa Carvalho or Marcos Portugal, composed expressly to be played on the Basilica's six organs.

d6d9c08d-bc42-54cc-90c2-ca572c64044c.name: Svatý Kopeček (Holy Hill)
d6d9c08d-bc42-54cc-90c2-ca572c64044c.description: Part of Cardinal Dietrichstein’s Counter-Reformation strategy was the construction of the Church of St. Sebastian on Tanzberg Hill. This pilgrimage church, with 13 chapels of the Stations of the Cross, was intended to turn a rocky hill, redolent with pagan legend, into a “Holy Mount” modelled on Varallo in northern Italy. The original church (G. G. Tencalla) was re-established after 1663 and in 18th and 19th centuries.

d721d07e-af8d-5c90-a2d1-60b3a0ac2fd3.name: Altar of the Holy Kinship
d721d07e-af8d-5c90-a2d1-60b3a0ac2fd3.description: The Altar of the Holy Family (or more broadly the Holy Kinship), with its altarpiece, is a reference to the Bavarian dynasty and the future of Christian Bavaria. The theme of the Annunciation of the Virgin is carried through in the imagery of the altar; the painting, the figures of saints either side, and the predella panel at the bottom. The altar can be seen therefore to indicate the birth of the Crown Prince and reiterate the dedicational background of the church. At one time the altarpiece in the choir (now destroyed) also picked up on this votive purpose.

d8eb5e02-b29c-5131-ae4d-9d51da74a14f.name: *St. Charles Borromeo*, *St. Roch*, *St Francis Xavier* and *St. John Nepomuk* (detail)

da8631fc-2904-5fa9-8e88-60dc987c0a59.name: *St. Francis Xavier* (detail)
da8631fc-2904-5fa9-8e88-60dc987c0a59.location: Upper inner rim of the monument

dd9d98d4-ce14-5cb3-81aa-86c331412c4e.name: Altar of St. Frances Borgia
dd9d98d4-ce14-5cb3-81aa-86c331412c4e.description: The Altar of St. Francis Borgia is characterised by its conservative, two-storey architectural structure with symmetrically deployed statues. The caryatids of the bottom, the spiral columns, and the acanthus ornaments – which were actually first brought by Komersteiner to Zagreb and northern Croatia in the 1680s – introduce Baroque accents into the church. On the Altar of St. Franics Borgia, softly rounded acanthus leaves sparsely furnish the load-bearing areas and mouldings, more abundantly on the narrow wings. The design of the altarpiece is attributed to H. A. Weissenkircher.
dd9d98d4-ce14-5cb3-81aa-86c331412c4e.location: The first side chapel of St. Frances Borgia on the right-hand (south) side of the nave

e6d1474a-473c-5669-a0d5-a4ba232d0192.name: Interior, facing east
e6d1474a-473c-5669-a0d5-a4ba232d0192.description: The actual sacred centre of the church is the Chapel of Mercy with the devotional picture of Mary, an oval structure at the central axis of the nave. The hall of the church is surmounted by a depressed barrel vault in which deep lunettes are cut. The walls are structured by simple pilasters. The heavily retracted choir of steeper proportions receives considerably more light than the nave and thus stages the high altar as the second focal point of the space, opposite the Chapel of Mercy.

e88898ac-b98e-5bad-81d8-2344a9fd7fed.name: Angel pointing to the Virgin with Child
e88898ac-b98e-5bad-81d8-2344a9fd7fed.description: The beautiful side angels made by Mazza for the former altar were reused in this new version with the help of the sculptor himself.

e9b3c366-6e58-520e-b2f0-8115391ee915.name: High altar
e9b3c366-6e58-520e-b2f0-8115391ee915.description: This altar is typically baroque with its elegant curved lines and its open shape, embracing the space. It is a good example of different artistic techniques (sculpture, architectural painting, architecture and figural painting) and of different materials (stucco, painted and gilded wood, fresco, and oil on canvas). It is perfectly in harmony with the space of the church blending the frescoes on the ceiling, the elegant balustrade, the organs and side pillars. This imposing altar frames a fresco fragment of the Virgin with Child, worshipped in the church of Santa Maria di Galliera since the fifteenth-century. The church was completely remodelled in the eighteenth-century and the main altar was rebuilt twice. Giuseppe Maria Mazza built the first version between 1691, when the Filippines fathers inherited a large sum of money in order to refurbish the main chapel, and 1706, when the decoration is mentioned in a guidebook for the first time. This altar, made of stucco, looked like great curtain suspended to the wall and held by two angels and some putti. Before 1739 the decoration was destroyed in order to build a new altar which was designed by Francesco Bibiena. This altar was decorated with two wooden statues of Justice and Peace, carved by the Tuscan Silvestro Giannotti, and two putti, moulded by Angelo Gabriello Piò. The central part of the altar is decorated with a picture by Giuseppe Rolli of angels carrying the medieval Madonna and Child, framed by a rich baroque carving.
e9b3c366-6e58-520e-b2f0-8115391ee915.artist: Francesco Bibiena, Giuseppe Maria Mazza, Giuseppe Rolli, Angelo Gabriello Piò, Silvestro Giannotti

eb2c6bd8-523c-5da1-ab39-330d09fffdc5.name: The Triumph of Intelligence over Brutality
eb2c6bd8-523c-5da1-ab39-330d09fffdc5.description: The Triumph of Intelligence, represented as Minerva, over Brutality, symbolized by the Giants.

ef97269c-7f1c-524a-b766-0796d7d80956.name: *Apotheosis of the Work of St. Ignatius*
ef97269c-7f1c-524a-b766-0796d7d80956.description: The central figure of St. Ignatius is painted most probably after a print depicting the marble statue of the saint made by Camillo and Giuseppe Rusconi in 1733 for the Basilica of St. Peter’s in Rome.

f16e1653-232d-58b1-9c5a-9e463ced20a3.name: The Baptism of Christ
f16e1653-232d-58b1-9c5a-9e463ced20a3.description: The vault of the nave is roofed by a celestial sphere abounding in figures of saints and angels carrying symbols of the Old and New Testament. The central motif is the Baptism of Christ, while the scenes by the ledge are from the life of St. John; the composition culminates in a figure of God the Father. The vaults of the altar niches feature framed scenes with the patron saints, to which individual altars are dedicated. As is typical of Etgens, the decorative components – cartouches, decorative vases and illusionary architecture – are essential:  The monumental fresco is the final work of this prominent Moravian artist. The church decoration was completed by J. Stern.

f2c3e5c1-e11f-5d98-af35-9b30d507c062.name: High altar
f2c3e5c1-e11f-5d98-af35-9b30d507c062.description: The high altar includes a picture of the Saviour (*Salvatore*) given blessing in Laterano, near Rome, where the original is to be found. In front of the high altar are two tombstones covering the entrance to an underground crypt. The right one commemorates F. M. Šubíř of Chobyně founder of the church, the left one his wife and children. On a side altar to the left is a glass coffin containing the remnants of St. Felician, a martyr from the period of the first Christians, which was acquired in 1735. On the right is an altar of tools of the Lord's martyrdom with a replica of the Turin Shroud. The ceiling painting is modern.
f2c3e5c1-e11f-5d98-af35-9b30d507c062.location: Interior, Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka

f2e3163a-4308-51ca-8274-354207600f17.name: General view of the Sacristy
f2e3163a-4308-51ca-8274-354207600f17.description: The redesigned sacristy with marble floor and a marble table. The coat of arms of the Franciscans and of the Royal family are fashioned in *Azulejos,* above which are a series of paintings with religious themes. A Brazilian ebony chest of drawers with a Rococo gilded carved back furnishes one end.
f2e3163a-4308-51ca-8274-354207600f17.artist: Woodcarver: Félix Adauto da Cunha (1649–c.1703); painter André Gonçalves (1685–1762)

f2fd7abc-465f-5f55-a1af-5082af90fafa.name: Sacristy
f2fd7abc-465f-5f55-a1af-5082af90fafa.description: The sacristy holds a large chest of drawers form the 17th century. On its wooden back board is a set of 20 paintings from the Life of St. Francis Xavier.
f2fd7abc-465f-5f55-a1af-5082af90fafa.location: Church interior, Sacristy, Church of São Roque

f3472803-8a49-5d58-b72d-b03b7f910c1b.name: “Amtshof” or the Ceremonial Courtyard
f3472803-8a49-5d58-b72d-b03b7f910c1b.description: In 1719 a fire destroyed the chateau interiors. Reconstruction was undertaken by C. A. Oedtl, who unified the chateau complex with a single frontage. He also rebuilt several other houses in the town. A ballroom was converted into a winter riding hall, and the theatre hall was reconstructed into a library; a *sala terrena* with a terrace was added and the ceremonial courtyard was refurbished, lined with busts of ancient emperors, and further decorated with *putti* and ornamental vases. The wrought-iron gates by H. G. Forster are original.
f3472803-8a49-5d58-b72d-b03b7f910c1b.artist: Christian Alexander Oedtl (1654 Paznaun – 1731 Vienna), Ignaz Lengelacher (1698 Unter Peissenberg – 1780 Baden), Heinrich Gottfried Forster

f78d544f-2dff-5ee2-bb44-142887c4b8d2.name: *St. Roch* (detail)
f78d544f-2dff-5ee2-bb44-142887c4b8d2.location: Upper inner rim of the monument

f9e1619f-ad4c-5283-96ab-edde611f3de0.name: The Baptism of Christ
f9e1619f-ad4c-5283-96ab-edde611f3de0.description: The high altarpiece, supplied by a professor of the Vienna Academy, M. Unterberger, was hailed as the best in Moravia at the time. It is framed by statues of the Prophets Isaiah and Zachary, father of John the Baptist, which are mirror transcriptions of the Apostles Peter and Paul in the Rajhrad Monastery Church. Two *bozzetos* for these monumental statues by I. Lengelacher have survived (Moravian Gallery), and may well have provided direct inspiration for the Kroměříž statues. Volute consoles hold allegories of the Old and New Testaments. Unterberger also painted the two side altarpieces.
f9e1619f-ad4c-5283-96ab-edde611f3de0.artist: Michelangelo Unterberger (1695 Cavalese – 1758 Vienna), Wolfgang Träger (1714 Pilsen – 1763 Olomouc)

fb69020a-86ca-5884-8fbe-a4756b55b391.name: St. Fidelius of Sigmaringen
fb69020a-86ca-5884-8fbe-a4756b55b391.description: This picture of St. Fidelius of Sigmaringen was first painted by Kracker for the Capuchin Monastery in Znojmo. Sandrart lived in the monastery before being summoned to work for the Bishop of Jager. The Brno piece was probably an unfinished painting by J. T. Rotter in whose workshop Kracker worked after graduating from the Vienna Academy.
fb69020a-86ca-5884-8fbe-a4756b55b391.location: Capuchin Monastery and the Church of the Invention of the Holy Cross, Brno

fc094f04-ed4e-5c5a-b47f-7bcc11b75d8f.name: The Chapel of Santo António  or Ante-Choir
fc094f04-ed4e-5c5a-b47f-7bcc11b75d8f.description: The beautiful floors of the Chapel of Santo António are of inlaid Brazilian wood. *Azulejo* panels – representing scenes from the lives of the hermit saints Anthony and Paul – adorn the walls on the lower register, while on the upper register are paintings depicting the Miracles of St Anthony of Lisbon. Behind a monumental door is the Madre de Deus crib, comprising a set of 42 sculpted polychrome terracotta figures.
fc094f04-ed4e-5c5a-b47f-7bcc11b75d8f.artist: André Gonçalves (1685–1762); terracotta figures in crib: António Ferreira [n.d.] and Dionísio Ferreira [n.d.]

fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.name: Frontage
fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.description: The convex-concave frontage traces the ground plan. The blind central entrance is particularly remarkable certainly holding symbolic meaning and probably embodying the third gate of St. John’s Revelation. Stone coats of arms of the church’s founder and his wife appear above the staircase, while a central cartouche features the bull of Pope Clement XI. Ledges that sit above crosses in shallow niches may symbolise Christ’s crown of thorns.
fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Elevation of the Holy Cross, Jaroměřice u Jevíčka
fc8fe75f-aa42-5aa6-8958-3321f68494d9.artist: František Benedikt Klíčník? (1677 Ivanovice na Hané – 1755 Brno)

ff2f7e9c-b837-54ae-88c0-9b70a0b56098.name: Monastic wings
ff2f7e9c-b837-54ae-88c0-9b70a0b56098.description: The newly renovated large corridors of these wings portray the eloquence of the great baroque monastic spaces, not due to the excessive ornamentations, but rather due to its size, its infinite passages and the repetitive and monotonous spans of the cells with its partition walls.
